items.title: Strategy halts Bitcoin buying and pivots to selling
points: Strategy has sold 6,948 BTC since May, worth roughly $433 million, reversing its original 'never sell' mandate.
A new 'capital management framework' (an internal policy setting rules for how the company uses its cash and assets) permits up to $1.25 billion in total BTC sales.
Proceeds are going to cash reserves and buybacks of its STRC preferred shares (shares that pay a fixed dividend and rank ahead of common stock).
No new Bitcoin purchases since June, suspending the long-term accumulation strategy indefinitely.
Bitcoin held flat near $63,500, staying in the $63,000–$64,000 range despite the liquidations.

items.title: Prediction markets slash odds of Strategy hitting 1 million BTC
points: Myriad (a prediction market owned by Decrypt's parent company Dastan) now gives just 6% odds Strategy reaches 1 million BTC by end of 2026, down sharply from prior expectations.
The drop reflects fading confidence in the Bitcoin treasury narrative (public companies stockpiling BTC on their balance sheets) after the pivot to selling.
The 1M BTC milestone had been viewed as a marquee institutional adoption signal.

items.title: Ethereum roadmap pivots to quantum resistance and AI verification
points: Vitalik Buterin's updated technical roadmap puts quantum resistance (protection against future quantum computers that could break today's cryptography) at the center of long-term development.
Privacy upgrades and AI-assisted formal verification (using machine learning to mathematically prove code is bug-free) are also priorities.
Signals Ethereum is preparing for both emerging computational threats and AI tooling in smart contract development.

items.title: Dormant Bitcoin wallet wakes after 12+ years
points: An address inactive for over 12 years moved 26.96 BTC worth about $1.75 million.
Adds to a growing pattern of long-dormant early Bitcoin addresses reactivating.

items.title: Other headlines
points: North Korea is increasingly relying on organized crime networks to launder stolen crypto.
Wall Street is starting to treat local opposition to data centers as a credit risk in lending decisions.

Prediction markets now give only 6% odds that Strategy reaches 1 million BTC by year-end, down sharply from prior expectations as the treasury narrative faces headwinds.
Bitcoin trades flat near $63,500 despite Strategy's major sales, suggesting the market has absorbed the selling pressure without significant impact on price.
Ethereum's roadmap pivots toward quantum-resistant cryptography and AI-assisted verification as core technical priorities moving forward.

sections.title: Strategy's Bitcoin Sales and Strategic Shift
points: Strategy has sold 6,948 BTC since May, worth approximately $433 million, marking a dramatic reversal from its original 'never sell' mandate.

The company adopted a 'capital management framework' allowing up to $1.25 billion in total BTC sales, with proceeds used to shore up cash reserves and fund stock buybacks of its preferred shares (STRC).
No new Bitcoin purchases have occurred since June, indicating the firm's long-term accumulation strategy has been suspended indefinitely.
Despite these large sales, Bitcoin price has remained stable in the $63,000–$64,000 range, with markets appearing indifferent to Strategy's liquidations.

sections.title: Market Sentiment and 1 Million BTC Target
points: Prediction market Myriad (owned by Decrypt's parent company Dastan) now assigns only 6% probability to Strategy reaching 1 million BTC by the end of 2026, down from much higher expectations.
The shift in odds reflects diminished confidence in the Bitcoin treasury narrative following the company's pivot to selling rather than accumulating.
This milestone was previously seen as a major institutional Bitcoin adoption signal; its reduced likelihood signals changing market sentiment on corporate crypto holdings.

sections.title: Ethereum's Quantum and AI Security Roadmap
points: Vitalik Buterin outlined an updated Ethereum technical roadmap placing quantum resistance (protection against future quantum computing threats) at the center of long-term development.
The roadmap also prioritizes privacy improvements and AI-assisted formal verification (using machine learning to prove code correctness automatically).
These shifts suggest Ethereum is preparing for both emerging computational threats and the integration of advanced AI tooling into smart contract development.
